page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-48-lssd is a general-purpose, storage-equipped server instance powered by the arm64 architecture. It features 48 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor, operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz with a single thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is bundled with 4020 GB of NVMe SSD capacity across 10 local drives, while offering zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and no GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier status in Geekbench multi-core scores, software compilation with Clang, Passmark memory performance, and Passmark database operations. Static web serving throughput is also in the top tier, reaching 97.21 GB/sec. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and memory bandwidth metrics fall within the strong category. Conversely, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and Passmark CPU encryption testing placing in the average category.

The c4a-standard-48-lssd offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that can leverage parallel ARM processing and high-speed local NVMe storage. The dedicated physical core allocation ensures consistent compute performance without virtualization overhead. However, the lack of hyperthreading and average single-core benchmark results represent a tradeoff for single-threaded tasks. The high-capacity local SSD configuration provides excellent read and write performance but requires application-level data replication due to the ephemeral nature of local NVMe storage.

This instance fits database operations, high-throughput web serving, and software compilation pipelines. The combination of top-tier database benchmarks, rapid memory bandwidth, and 4020 GB of local NVMe SSD makes it an effective platform for distributed databases, caching layers like Redis, and large-scale static web hosting. It is also applicable for multi-threaded development workflows, such as CI/CD compilation, and medium-scale language model inference tasks.
